description.text:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development.
It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways,
without incrementing the interface major version and without prior
notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients
and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols
and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or
semantics remaining stable across releases.

This protocol allows general applications to query and receive live
notifications for user-level appearance settings managed by the
compositor, including cursor theme and size, fonts (proportional,
monospace, size), and visual appearance (icon theme, accent color,
window opacity, color scheme, titlebar height, and corner radius).

Any client may bind this interface. The compositor pushes the current
value of every setting immediately after the client binds this global,
and broadcasts events to all bound clients whenever a setting changes.

The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are
to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.
description.summary: query and observe user-level appearance settings

description.text:
A singleton global for observing user-level appearance settings
of the current user. These settings are shared by all windows
and clients of the user rather than being per-window. Each
bound client receives events reporting the initial values of
all settings immediately after binding, and subsequent events
whenever any setting changes.

Destroy the treeland_appearance_v1 object. The
compositor will no longer send events on this object after
this request.

Emitted by the compositor when the cursor theme changes.
Also emitted immediately after binding to report the
current theme.

Emitted by the compositor when the cursor size changes.
Also emitted immediately after binding to report the
current size in pixels. Width and height may differ on
hardware that supports non-square cursor planes.

Emitted when the proportional font family changes.
Also emitted immediately after binding to report the current
font.

Emitted when the monospace font family changes.
Also emitted immediately after binding to report the current
font.

Emitted when the base font size changes.
Also emitted immediately after binding to report the current
size in points multiplied by 10.

args.name: size
args.summary: current font size in points multiplied by 10

description.text:
Emitted when the icon theme changes. Also emitted
immediately after binding to report the current theme.

Emitted when the accent color changes. Also emitted
immediately after binding to report the current color.
Color components are unsigned values in the range [0, 255].

Emitted when the global window background opacity changes.
Also emitted immediately after binding to report the current
value. The value is a fixed-point value in the range [0.0, 1.0].

Emitted when the color scheme hint changes. Also
emitted immediately after binding to report the current
scheme. Clients should restyle their self-drawn components
whenever this event is received.

Emitted when the compositor titlebar height changes. Also
emitted immediately after binding to report the current
value in pixels.

args.name: height
args.summary: current compositor titlebar height in pixels

description.text:
Emitted when the global default corner radius changes.
Also emitted immediately after binding to report the current
value in pixels.
description.summary: global window corner radius has changed

args.name: radius
args.summary: current global corner radius in pixels

description.text:
A user-level hint for the preferred color scheme. Clients
should use this value to style their self-drawn widgets and
UI elements accordingly. The compositor also applies this
hint to server-side decorations. This is semantically
equivalent to org.freedesktop.appearance color-scheme and
the CSS prefers-color-scheme media feature.

This enum mirrors treeland_appearance_manager_v1.color_scheme
(in the privileged treeland-appearance-manager-unstable-v1
protocol): the entry names and values are identical and must
stay in sync. Any new value must be added to both at once.
